utility.notes: Naperville operates its own municipal electric utility, distinct from ComEd or Ameren Illinois — a genuinely non-trivial fact, since a nearby suburb could easily be assumed (incorrectly) to be ComEd/Ameren territory without checking. Interconnection and net metering for Naperville residents are handled directly by the City's own Electric Utility, not a third-party investor-owned utility.

value.name: Naperville Electric Utility
value.notes: Municipal utility — recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Naperville spans both DuPage and Will counties; the majority of the city and its municipal building/electric-utility jurisdiction is treated as DuPage County for this record. Regardless of county, Naperville's own Building Department and Electric Utility — not the county — are the permitting/interconnection authorities within city limits.

permit_authority.notes: Illinois has no single statewide residential solar permitting rule — permitting authority sits with the local municipality (inside its boundaries) or the county (in unincorporated areas). Naperville's own Building Department issues the building permit; a separate Interconnection Agreement with Naperville Electric Utility is also required.

battery_programs.notes: No dedicated battery/storage-specific incentive program was found on Naperville's own pages this session, distinct from the rooftop-solar rebate recorded under rebates.

value.name: Naperville Rooftop Solar Incentive (Residential Energy Efficiency Incentives program)
value.description: A residential rebate for a roof-mounted solar array or a solar water heater system, administered alongside Naperville's other residential energy-efficiency incentives (attic insulation, single-pane window replacement, AC tune-up, furnace blower motor replacement) under a single shared annual budget. As of 2026-06-26, the City's own page states the program's $280,000 total annual budget across all of these incentive categories (including Rooftop Solar) has been 100% awarded, and applications are closed for the remainder of the 2026 calendar year. Third-party sources report a rate of $250 per kW AC (inverter-rated), capped at $1,750 (7 kW AC max) and requiring a $5/month, 5-year contribution to the Naperville Renewable Energy Program — this specific dollar figure was not independently confirmed from a City of Naperville page fetched this session and should be verified directly before relying on it.
value.eligibility: Customer-owned systems only (leased systems ineligible); 100% complete application must be submitted within 120 days of passing final inspection; no incentive is awarded until the project is complete, operational, and has passed final inspection.

rebates.notes: Status recorded as 'unknown' (not 'active' or 'expired') because the program's annual budget was confirmed exhausted for 2026 as of the City's own 2026-06-26 update, but the City's page frames this as a recurring annual budget rather than a permanently discontinued program — whether it reopens with new funding in a subsequent calendar year was not stated. This is a genuine current funding-exhaustion status, honestly preserved rather than presented as an open incentive.
